rows.34:25d4:
When she went through the old graduation albums, she found Okazaki right away.
Her full name was Yukie Okazaki.
She had been a student about twenty-five years before Okawa.
That Okazaki had known about Rubelize so long ago, and had even owned it, filled Okawa with bitter resentment.
Back then, power stones weren't even something ordinary people talked about.
That's just how selfish people are.{p}Naturally, you can guess what Okawa had in mind, can't you?
rows.34:42e8:
Thinking such things, she wandered out of the school in despair, unsteady on her feet.
And she was caught in a traffic accident.
She was struck by an oncoming car and killed instantly.
They say even after she breathed her last, she was still clutching the pendant that brought happiness.
That Rubelize power stone.
This came out afterward, but by then the organ was already gone from this world.
On her father's orders, the organ hadn't been sold; it had been destroyed.
The teacher couldn't bear to say so and lied that it had been sold.
But that lie led to her death.
The organ went to heaven, and she followed after it, to where the organ was.
I wonder if she's playing the organ in heaven now.
For the angels who died young...{p}
rows.34:4958:
I think graveyards are frightening even in the daytime.
And this was the middle of the night.
A high school girl, all alone.
That's not something just anyone could do.
And her purpose was grave robbing, at that.
Okawa must have had nerves of steel.
Or perhaps the Rubelize sleeping in the grave was calling her to it.
Heh heh...
Either way, she moved the gravestone aside and took Okazaki's urn out from inside.
And when she opened the urn... there it was.{p}
rows.34:61b4:
She was a girl from a perfectly ordinary family.
But apparently the son and heir of a certain wealthy zaibatsu family gave her a Rubelize.
They say even at the prices back then it cost as much as a house, so it was a present far beyond anything we'd think of as normal.
The zaibatsu boy's name was Hideto Fujiomi.
Fujiomi had been in love with Okazaki for a long time, without her returning it.
He gave her the Rubelize and confessed, asking her to go out with him.
Okazaki was a very pretty girl.
She had a distinctive kind of cuteness, the kind that could have made her an idol.
Her classmates were all envious.
Back then, no one yet cared that the Rubelize was a stone that brings happiness.
But since it was a rare stone even by world standards, it seems it became the talk of the school.
So the girls who told Okawa about her must have heard that rumor from somewhere too.{p}
rows.34:683c:
The answers were faintly rising to the surface of her answer sheet.
(Wh-what is this...?)
She was astonished.
It didn't take her long to realize it was the Rubelize's power.
"How was it?
The test?"
The moment the test was over, Fujiomi came straight over to talk to her.
Okazaki answered him with trembling lips.
"It really worked..."
Seeing the state she was in, Fujiomi smiled with satisfaction.
And he slowly nodded.{p}
rows.34:75f0:
I'm the one who stole the Rubelize.
Only you and I know about the Rubelize's power, right?
So I decided to shut you up.
From here on, I'm going to graduate from a good university and land a good job.
With the stone's power.
I was worried that using the stone's power might bring something horrible as the price, but...
it looks like that's not a problem.
With the test, and when we changed the weather, nothing bad happened to you, and you were the one making the wishes.
Now I'll put my real goal to the test.
Okazaki.
I want to kill you.{p}
rows.34:83b0:
...But Okawa couldn't give up.
So at last she made up her mind.
She would secretly dig up Okazaki's grave.
What kind of nerve did she have, I wonder?
She seemed to think it was fine to steal from the dead as long as no one found out.
Okawa waited for the dead of night, then put her plan into action.{p}
rows.34:a3b0:
They say she was found dead, her mouth stuffed full of something like ash.
No doubt that ash was...{p}
rows.34:cee0:
I'm your real mother.
Let me play the organ for you.
After all, I parted from my husband when you were still just a baby.
Let me play you a lullaby.
My sweet Yukie..."
Okazaki grew sleepier and sleepier.{p}
